findings.F1: The test's slope is on the predicted side but small: t 1.33 on 2489 positive-forecast grid cases. Within those cases the forecast is not graded: mean excess 5-day returns by forecast quintile are -0.11 %, +0.52 %, +0.01 %, +0.63 % and +0.72 %, each with t ≤ 1.41. What separates is a positive forecast against a zero one: +0.35 % against -0.38 % excess, with the top 40 % of the forecast minus flat at Welch t 2.50.
findings.F2: The supporting check passed because of the coin's own short-term reversal, not because of the idea. Over all grid bars, whatever the forecast, prior 5-day return ≤ 0 minus > 0 gives +0.35 % minus -0.40 %, Welch t 2.34 on 4602 cases. Regressing the positive cases' excess 5-day return on both the forecast and the prior 5-day return gives t -2.68 for the prior return and t 1.31 for the forecast (2372 cases).
findings.F3: The idea's modulation runs the other way. The forecast's slope t is 0.35 after a 5-day fall (1183 cases) and 1.46 after a 5-day rise (1189 cases).
findings.F4: The slope changes sign across periods and coins.
findings.F5: The idea is small against the coin's normal moves, and there is little left to scale.
findings.F6: Other horizons do not show the effect. On each horizon's own non-overlapping grid the slope t is 0.37 at 10 days (1234 cases), 0.91 at 15 days, 0.14 at 20 days (604 cases) and -0.09 at 30 days.
findings.F7: The prior 5-day return alone is graded among the positive-forecast cases. By prior-return quintile, from the lowest (mean prior return -13.8 %) to the highest (+14.2 %), the excess 5-day return is +1.11 % (t 1.99), +0.26 %, +0.77 %, -0.06 % and -0.47 %.

ideas.same-idea-on: instruments: BTC, ETH, LTC, XMR, XRP, ZEC, ADA, DOGE, LINK, TRX, UNI, AAVE, AVAX, SOL, INJ, NEAR, SUI, TAO, ONDO; bar: 1d; period: folds A, B, C, D
ideas.name: nearness reversal, all coins
ideas.idea: For a coin's nearness to its 90-day high, the larger both the excess of its past 365-day predictive power for 5-day returns and today's deviation of nearness from its usual level, when the reading points against a past relation that implies a fall, the larger the coin's rise over the next 5 days. This rise is larger the lower the coin's own 5-day return before the reading.
ideas.consequence: A trader should take the long nearness-power reversal on coins that have not just risen over the last 5 days, and skip it after a 5-day run-up, where its edge turns negative.

ideas.idea: The lower a coin's own 5-day return, the larger its rise over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader should lean long on a coin in proportion to how far it has fallen over the last 5 days, and refuse longs after a 5-day run-up.
ideas.name: five-day fall reverses
